svg.title: Five disciplines, and what each one actually engineers
svg.desc: Five layers stacked. Data engineering engineers the table, and without it the model has nothing true to reason over. Prompt engineering engineers the instruction, and without it the model does the wrong task well. Context engineering engineers what enters the window, and without it the model is fluent and uninformed. Loop engineering engineers the iteration, and without it the model gets one attempt at a multi-step problem. Harness engineering engineers the scaffolding across model versions, and without it you keep paying for workarounds the model no longer needs. Each layer assumes the one beneath it.
svg.text: Harness engineering
Unit of work: the scaffolding, across model versions
Evaluate, then subtract. Delete what the model no longer needs.
Skip it and you keep paying for last year's workarounds.
Loop engineering
Unit of work: the iteration
Plan, act, observe, retry, escalate to a human, stop.
Skip it and the model gets one attempt at a multi-step problem.
Context engineering
Unit of work: what enters the window
Retrieve, rank, assemble, trim, ground in a real query.
Skip it and the model is fluent and uninformed.
Prompt engineering
Unit of work: the instruction
Say what the task is, in what shape, with what constraints.
Skip it and the model does the wrong task, well.
Data engineering
Unit of work: the table
Ingest, store, transform, serve. Governed and current.
Skip it and there is nothing true for the model to reason over.
Each layer assumes the one beneath it. You cannot buy your way past a missing floor —
most failed agent projects are a layer-1 problem wearing a layer-4 budget.
